items.title: Unregulated peptide popularity prompts cancer warning
items.description: Skin specialists are sounding a warning about the potential cancer risks associated with unregulated peptides at the heart of a social media-driven beauty craze.

items.title: Australia's greenhouse gas emissions drop as renewable energy, batteries surge
items.description: Emissions are at their lowest point since the COVID pandemic shut down the economy, dropping 2.1 per cent over the year to December 2025.

items.title: Debate over house prices 'invokes terror' in politicians
items.description: Politicians have been hesitant to say whether prices should rise or fall, as both sides of politics feel the pressure of trying to appease voters who own and voters who are trying to buy.

items.title: Australian beef could be hit by 55 per cent tariff in China within days
items.description: China is cracking down on beef imports and says it is ready to slap Australia with an additional 55 per cent tariff in the coming days.

items.title: Lack of services for Kumanjayi Little Baby forced her family to live in town
items.description: Member for Lingiari Marion Scrymgour says the mother of Kumanjayi Little Baby had been living in insecure housing in Alice Springs so she could access specialist support for her daughter, before the five-year-old's tragic death in April.

items.title: The race against time to contain Ebola
items.description: Tensions are running high as officials fight to stop the rapid spread of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where aid workers tell the ABC they are already playing catch-up with the deadly disease.

items.title: Tantric workshops, couple swaps and toys: Intimacy pressures on MAFS exposed
items.description: Married At First Sight UK has become the centre of rape allegations. Now former MAFS Australia contestants and producers are speaking out about being coerced into intimacy.

items.title: New bulk-billing contraceptive centres aim to combat information void
items.description: Misinformation, cost and a lack of trained providers have stopped many Australian women from accessing what doctors consider the most effective form of reversible contraception.

items.title: Bullock says RBA will re-tender KPMG whistleblower hotline contract amid scandals
items.description: The Reserve Bank is distancing itself from KPMG with Governor Michele Bullock confirming the bank will re-tender its whistleblower hotline service.

items.title: Why war has made Iran's leadership frictions more 'consequential'
items.description: A report about the resignation of Iran's president earlier this week came at a turbulent moment for Iran's regime, which is grappling with frictions between moderates and hardliners as the war drags on.

items.title: Fuel price expected to rise after excise cuts end on June 30
items.description: Experts say consumers have 30 days until they pay more at the pump if no peace deal is finalised in the Middle East and the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

items.title: Hanson takes the stage as Chalmers's budget woes roll on
items.description: While Labor is increasingly concerned about the long-term threat of One Nation, this week its attention was squarely on more immediate problems.

items.title: Ancient tribes, military, trade and China's rise meet on this island
items.description: India's Great Nicobar Island is home to one of the world's last isolated tribes who are believed to have lived there for thousands of years, but a rising China is set to see it undergo a major transformation at the Indian government's insistence.

items.title: Man presumed dead survives week on Mount Everest without food or oxygen
items.description: A Sherpa guide, presumed dead after failing to descend from Mount Everest, was found crawling down to base camp a week after he went missing.

items.title: Piastri hunting Monaco silverware to mark historic F1 milestone
items.description: On an historic occasion for one of Formula 1's most storied teams, Oscar Piastri is hoping to add silverware to McLaren's special day in Monaco.

items.title: ABC news quiz: Mystery markings, a premature celebration and a fight over the Big… something
items.description: You too could learn the dangers of celebrating too soon if you underestimate this week's news quiz.

items.title: A new documentary brings things home for the author of Dark Emu
items.description: A slow-cinema treasure, Grace McKenzie's documentary, Yumburra, traces author Bruce Pascoe's establishment of a farm.

items.title: The best fresh produce to shop for in June
items.description: Winter has arrived. This is some of the best seasonal produce to look for.

items.title: Wong says she believes activists who say they were sexually assaulted in Israeli custody
items.description: Foreign Minister Penny Wong has told a parliamentary hearing she believes the allegations of Australian activists, who say they were sexually assaulted while detained by Israeli forces.

items.title: Coach defends doctors as Crows players play out game after head clash
items.description: Matthew Nicks defends his medical staff after two Crows were cleared to play out their win against the Cats without a concussion test after a nasty head clash.

items.title: Souths stung by 'sticky spray' ruling as Manly continue Foran resurgence
items.description: The Manly Sea Eagles have provisionally moved into the NRL top four with a 28-14 win over the South Sydney Rabbitohs at Brookvale Oval.

items.title: Aussie 7s star has 'unfinished business' after injury ended 2024 Olympic debut
items.description: For an athlete still in the early stages of her professional career, Australian rugby 7s player Kaitlin Shave has already experienced the highs and lows of sport.

items.title: Public apology after Nepal's women's national team violates 'spirit of cricket'
items.description: Nepal's cricket board has offered a public apology after its women's team successfully had a batter timed out.

items.title: Teen's brutal death a flashpoint over violence against women and femicide
items.description: The alleged brutal murder of 14-year-old Agostina Vega in Argentina has reignited a generation-defining movement demanding justice for the women victims of crime and violence.

items.title: Bondi terror attack hero Ahmed Al Ahmed charged with assault
items.description: Mr Ahmed has been charged with domestic violence common assault after an incident in Bankstown in March.
